body: ## User Story  As a JoeKnock system administrator, I want geocoding requests controlled through the JoeKnock backend, so that the application does not expose or abuse the external geocoding service.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] Frontend does not call geocoding providers directly. - [ ] MVP geocoding flow is mediated through `POST /api/properties/resolve`. - [ ] Backend performs reverse geocoding as an internal implementation detail. - [ ] Requests require authentication. - [ ] Backend validates coordinates input. - [ ] Geocoding/provider behavior is handled behind JoeKnock API boundaries. - [ ] OpenStreetMap attribution requirements are supported by the application.  ## Technical Notes  - Public geocoding endpoints are not exposed in MVP. - Geocoding provider calls remain internal to backend property resolution. - Representatives do not manually edit latitude or longitude.  ## Related database tables  - properties  ## Related API endpoints  - POST /api/properties/resolve  ## Related ADRs  - Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`). - ADR-016: OpenStreetMap Nominatim for MVP Geocoding  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] Geocoding access remains backend-mediated and authentication-protected. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.

As a sales representative,
I want my interaction information protected when connectivity is interrupted,
so that I do not lose information while working in the field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Failed API requests are detected.
- [ ] User receives an understandable error message.
- [ ] Local interaction draft remains available.
- [ ] User can retry submission.
- [ ] Retry behavior does not create duplicate interaction outcomes.

- Preserve local draft-first UX for unstable connectivity.
- Retry flows must preserve immutable snapshot rules and existing interaction-group identity.

body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want to update an interaction when information changes, so that the current record reflects the latest information while preserving the original history.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] User can edit an authorized interaction. - [ ] Interaction updates use `POST /api/interactions/:id`. - [ ] Existing snapshot field values are not overwritten. - [ ] New immutable snapshot is created. - [ ] New snapshot keeps the same `interaction_group_id`. - [ ] `initial_interaction_at` remains unchanged. - [ ] `changed_at` is updated on the new snapshot. - [ ] Previous snapshot is preserved and no interaction deletion occurs. - [ ] Existing notes are copied to the new snapshot unless changed by the representative.  ## Technical Notes  - One interaction history exists per organization + property + representative in MVP. - Returning to the same property updates existing interaction history rather than creating a new one. - Only owner representatives edit their interaction records; managers/admins are view-only on others.  ## Related database tables  - interactions - properties - users - statuses  ## Related API endpoints  - POST /api/interactions/:id  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag - Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`).  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] API behavior matches documented ownership and immutability rules. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.

body: ## User Story  As a sales representative, I want to select a location on the map and identify its address, so that I can record an interaction without manually entering the property address.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] User can select a location/property on the map. - [ ] Frontend sends selected coordinates to `POST /api/properties/resolve`. - [ ] Backend performs reverse geocoding as an internal implementation detail. - [ ] Backend receives the geocoded address and normalizes it for matching. - [ ] Backend checks for an existing property within the authenticated organization. - [ ] Existing property is returned when found. - [ ] New property is created and returned when no match exists. - [ ] Frontend does not call the geocoding provider directly. - [ ] Geocoding/provider errors are handled gracefully.  ## Technical Notes  - Use the finalized MVP property-resolution flow: coordinates -> reverse geocoding -> normalized address -> organization-scoped lookup/create -> resolved property. - The geocoder-returned address is the address JoeKnock uses in MVP. - Representatives do not manually edit latitude or longitude. - Preserve organization isolation for all property resolution behavior.  ## Related database tables  - properties  ## Related API endpoints  - POST /api/properties/resolve  ## Related ADRs  - ADR-001: Map-First Application Design - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions - Organization isolation is defined by API/schema contracts (`docs/api_endpoints.md`, `docs/table_Schema_decisions.md`). - ADR-016: OpenStreetMap Nominatim for MVP Geocoding  ## Definition of Done  - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.
